headline: Kawa, “leather”, is a specialization of 皮 (kawa, “skin”).

sources.quote: Specialization of 皮(かわ) (kawa, “skin”).

examples.ja: よい革は何年ももつものだ。
examples.en: Good leather will wear for years.

examples.ja: このバッグは革でできています。
examples.en: This bag is made of leather.

headline: Tsukiai is the stem of 付き合う (tsukiau, “keep company with”), equivalent to 付き (tsuki) plus 合い (ai).

sources.quote: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 付(つ)き合(あ)う (tsukiau, “keep company with; get along with”), equivalent to 付(つ)き (tsuki) + 合(あ)い (ai).

examples.ja: 彼はつきあいが悪い。
examples.en: He is unsociable.

examples.ja: 彼はつきあいが広い。
examples.en: He has a lot of acquaintances.

headline: Katazuke is the continuative stem of 片付ける (katazukeru, “to tidy up”).

sources.quote: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 片付(かたづ)ける (katazukeru, “to tidy up”).

examples.ja: 彼女は食事の後片付けをした。
examples.en: She cleared away the dishes from the table.

examples.ja: 会議で使った書類の片づけを頼まれた。
examples.en: I was asked to put away all the papers we used at the meeting.

headline: Jūyō is Middle Chinese 重要, literally “heavy + important”.

sources.quote: /djuːeu/ → /d͡ʑuːeu/ → /d͡ʑuːjoː/
From Middle Chinese compound 重要 (drjowng^X ʔjiewᴴ, literally “heavy + important”).

examples.ja: 量より質が重要だ。
examples.en: Quality is more important than quantity.

examples.ja: 重要な役を演じる。
examples.en: I play an important part.

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Hadaka was originally 肌 (hada, “skin”) plus 赤 (aka, “red”).

sources.quote: /fada aka/ → /fadaka/ → /hadaka/
Originally a compound of 肌 (hada, “skin”) + 赤 (aka, “red”).

headline: Isamashii is 勇む (isamu) plus しい (-shii).

sources.quote: 勇(いさ)む (isamu) + しい (-shii)

examples.ja: 彼女は勇ましかった。
examples.en: She was brave.

examples.ja: 一人で原始林へ乗り込もうとは君はなんて勇ましいんだ。
examples.en: How brave of you to go alone into the primaeval forest!

headline: Mi is from Old Japanese, first attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese. First attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE in sense 1.

examples.ja: 木はその実で分かる。
examples.en: A tree is known by its fruit.

examples.ja: この実はたべられます。
examples.en: This berry is good to eat.

headline: Ritsu, “rate”, is from Middle Chinese 率 (MC lwit).

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 率 (MC lwit).

examples.ja: 彼は生産率を良くする案を出した。
examples.en: He put forward a plan for improving the rate of production.

examples.ja: 賭け率２対１でレッズが勝つだろう。
examples.en: The odds are two-to-one that the Reds win.

headline: Buki is from Middle Chinese 武器 (MC mjuX khijH).

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 武器 (MC mjuX khijH).

examples.ja: 彼は私に武器を向けた。
examples.en: He raised a weapon against me.

examples.ja: 涙は子供の武器である。
examples.en: Tears are a child's weapon.

headline: Tabemono is tabe, the stem of 食べる (taberu, “to eat”), plus 物 (-mono, “thing”).

sources.quote: Compound of 食(た)べ (tabe, “eating”, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 食(た)べる (taberu, “to eat”)) + 物(もの) (-mono, “thing”).

examples.ja: 食べ物が冷めます。
examples.en: The food is getting cold.

examples.ja: 食べ物は豊富にある。
examples.en: We have food in abundance.

headline: Hakari is the continuative stem of 量る (hakaru).

sources.quote: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 量(はか)る (hakaru).

examples.ja: 浴室の秤で体重を計った。
examples.en: I weighed myself on the bathroom scales.

examples.ja: 荷物をはかりの上にのせてください。
examples.en: Please put your baggage on this scale.

headline: Kenkyūshitsu is 研究 (kenkyū, “research”) plus 室 (-shitsu, “room”).

sources.quote: From 研究(けんきゅう) (kenkyū, “research”) + 室(しつ) (-shitsu, “room”).

examples.ja: 私たちはその研究室を利用した。
examples.en: We have made use of the laboratory.

examples.ja: 彼は自分の研究室で実験を行っている。
examples.en: He is carrying out experiments in his laboratory.

headline: Hanko comes from 版行 (hankō) > hanko.

sources.quote: From 版行 (hankō) > hanko.

headline: Kumiai went from kumiapi through kumiaɸi and kumiawi to kumiai.

sources.quote: /kumiahi/: *[kumiapi] → [kumiaɸi] → [kumiawi] → [kumiai].

examples.ja: 組合は無期限ストに入った。
examples.en: The union went out on a strike for an indefinite period.

examples.ja: 経営者側と組合は和解した。
examples.en: The management and the union were reconciled.

meaning: always, usually, every time, never (with neg. verb)
headline: Itsumo is いつ (itsu, “when”) plus も (mo, “even, also”).

sources.quote: From いつ (itsu, “when”) + も (mo, “even, also”).

headline: Kuyamu is derived from 悔いる (kuiru).

sources.quote: Derived from 悔いる (kuiru).

examples.ja: 今更悔やんでも後の祭りだ。
examples.en: It is too late to repent.

examples.ja: 彼はそのことをもう悔やんでいた。
examples.en: He was already regretting it.

headline: Ateru is from Old Japanese 当つ (atu), in the lower bigrade pattern.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese 当つ (atu), following 下二段活用 (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”).
Development

Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

examples.ja: 彼は的に当てた。
examples.en: He hit the mark.

examples.ja: 彼は額に手を当てた。
examples.en: He put his hand to his forehead.

headline: Kōkō contracts 高等学校 (kōtō-gakkō, “high school”).

sources.quote: Contraction of 高(こう)等(とう)学(がっ)校(こう) (kōtō-gakkō, “high school”).

examples.ja: 私は高校2年生だ。
examples.en: I am in the second year of high school.

examples.ja: 彼は高校の生徒です。
examples.en: He is a student at a high school.

headline: Kiri is the continuative stem of 切る (kiru, “to cut”).

sources.quote: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 切(き)る (kiru, “to cut”).

examples.ja: 彼は病気でずっと床についたきりだ。
examples.en: He has been confined to his bed with illness.

examples.ja: 彼は３８歳なのに両親に頼りきりです。
examples.en: Though 38, he is still dependent on his parents.

headline: Satsu, “bill”, is from Middle Chinese 札 (MC tsreat).

sources.quote: /satu/ → /sat͡su/
From Middle Chinese 札 (MC tsreat).

examples.ja: 五ドル札を崩せますか。
examples.en: Can you change a five-dollar bill?

examples.ja: １万円札くずれますか。
examples.en: Can you break a 10,000 yen bill?

headline: Shōbōsho is 消防 (shōbō, “fire fighting”) plus 署 (-sho, “station, office”).

sources.quote: From 消防(しょうぼう) (shōbō, “fire fighting”) + 署(しょ) (-sho, “station, office”).

examples.ja: 消防署に連絡してください。
examples.en: Please call the fire department.

examples.ja: 消防署は警察署の隣にあります。
examples.en: The fire station is next to the police station.

meaning: to fall behind, to be inferior to
headline: Otoru is cognate with 落ちる (ochiru, “to fall”), via an Old Japanese root ot-.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese 劣る (oto₂ru), from Proto-Japonic *ətəru, from Proto-Japonic *ət-.
Via Old Japanese root ot-, cognate with 落(お)ちる (ochiru, “to fall”, intransitive) and 落(お)とす (otosu, “to drop something”, transitive).

examples.ja: この点で私は彼に劣る。
examples.en: I fall behind him in this respect.

examples.ja: 彼は物理では誰にも劣らない。
examples.en: He is second to none in physics.

meaning: to move (from a house); to transfer (from a department); to shift
headline: Utsuru, “to move”, is cognate with 写る.

sources.quote: Cognate with Japanese 写る.

examples.ja: 事務所は６階に移った。
examples.en: The office has been transferred up to the sixth floor.

examples.ja: さて、次の話題に移ろう。
examples.en: But now to our next topic.

headline: Issakujitsu is 一昨 (issaku-, “the previous... before...”) plus 日 (jitsu, “day”), first cited to a text from 1275.

sources.quote: Compound of 一昨 (issaku-, “the previous... before...”) + 日 (jitsu, “day”).
First cited to a text from 1275.

headline: Sakari is the continuative stem of 盛る (sakaru).

sources.quote: The 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) of verb 盛る (sakaru).

examples.ja: 彼は今男盛りだ。
examples.en: He is now in the prime of manhood.

examples.ja: 桜花が盛りであった。
examples.en: The cherry blossoms were at their best.

meaning: terrible (in reference to food), unappetizing, unpleasant (taste)
headline: Mazui is derived from 貧しい (mazushii, “poor”).

sources.quote: Derived from 貧しい (mazushii, “poor”).

headline: Ine is attested in the Man'yōshū of circa 759 CE, and is possibly related to 米 (yone).

sources.quote: ⟨i₁ne⟩ → /ine/
From Old Japanese. Attested in the Man'yōshū of circa 759 CE. In turn, from Proto-Japonic *inay.
Possibly related to 米 (yone, “rice (husked grains of the Asian rice plant, Oryza sativa)”).

examples.ja: 今年は稲の育ちがいい。
examples.en: The rice is coming well this year.

examples.ja: 農夫達は稲を植えていた。
examples.en: The peasants were planting rice.

headline: Taisen is 大 (tai, “big, large”) plus 戦 (sen, “battle”).

sources.quote: Compound of 大(たい) (tai, “big, large”) + 戦(せん) (sen, “battle”).

examples.ja: あの家の繁栄は大戦中からのことだ。
examples.en: The prosperity of the family dates from the Great War.
